fields.title: Declaration of Local Emergency
whereas: on October 22, 2026, beginning at approximately 9:10 a.m., a cyberattack disabled the computer-aided dispatch, records management and radio console systems serving the Lakeshore County Emergency Communications Center; and

the same attack encrypted servers of the Milford Water Department, forcing manual operation of the Riverside Treatment Plant and placing the drinking water supply of approximately 84,000 residents at risk; and
911 calls are being answered and dispatched by hand, mutual aid is required from neighboring jurisdictions, and restoration is not expected for several days; and
the conditions threaten the life, health and safety of the people of Lakeshore County and are beyond the capacity of normal County services, personnel and equipment to address;
fields.declaration: I, Dana Whitfield, County Executive of Lakeshore County, by the authority vested in me by Chapter 12 (Emergency Management) of the Lakeshore County Code, do hereby declare that a local state of emergency exists throughout Lakeshore County, including the incorporated City of Milford.
powers: The Emergency Operations Plan is activated and the Director of Emergency Management shall staff the Emergency Operations Center and coordinate the response.
County departments may procure goods and services needed for the response without regard to normal bidding and procurement requirements; all such purchases shall be documented.
The Director is authorized to request and render mutual aid, and to request assistance from the State Office of Emergency Management and CISA.
Price gouging on water, fuel, generators and other essential goods is prohibited for the duration of this emergency.
Department heads may reassign personnel and suspend non-essential services as needed to support the response.
fields.authority: Chapter 12 (Emergency Management) of the Lakeshore County Code
fields.expires: seven (7) days from signing, at 6:45 p.m. on October 29, 2026
fields.ratification: This declaration shall be presented to the Lakeshore County Council for ratification at a special meeting called for that purpose, and may be extended only by resolution of the Council.
